messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT: CosmosHealth (VPC) — auth failures observed (OIDC/JWKS)
oncall-bot: Paging: @Maya R (primary oncall), @Samir K (secondary) — severity 1 — 2134567890
Maya R: I got it, looking. Symptoms?
CosmosAdmin (CosmosHealth): Seeing 401s across our Redwood VPC endpoints starting ~08:34 UTC. A few requests succeed and then fail. No recent config changes from our side except a scheduled JWKS rollover at 07:50.
Maya R: thanks. Can you share the kid values before/after and your jwks url?
CosmosAdmin (CosmosHealth): jwks: https://id.cosmoshealth.example/.well-known/jwks.json. Old kid: "k1-rcv", new kid: "k2-rot". Rotation completed at 07:51 and we validated tokens locally.
Samir K: getting logs from the auth-bridge in the Cosmos VPC cluster. Seeing: `jwt validation failed: kid not found` and repeated fetch attempts hitting our jwks cache TTL.
Eli T: I’m seeing the same in dedicated-pool-proxy logs: `GET /.well-known/jwks.json returned 200 but keys parse mismatch` followed by 401 to gateway. Looks like our JWKS cache didn’t pick up the new keys.
Maya R: any indication of a race between our key-cache refresh job and the customer rotation?
Samir K: yes — cache refresh interval is 6m, but we also have an in-memory cache that only refreshes if the kid in incoming token is unknown. If the new tokens arrive before the background refresh and with kid=k2-rot we try lookup -> fail -> 401.
Rachel S: did the auth-bridge emit a cache-bypass request to the jwks url?
Samir K: not initially. Our bridge respects `Cache-Control`/ETag and will back off. The customer’s jwks endpoint had aggressive caching headers on the CDN which prevented our fetch. So two contributors: customer's jwks published but CDN TTL stuck, and our in-memory cache/backoff logic suppressed immediate re-fetch.
Maya R: immediate mitigation options?
Eli T: we can force a cache clear for the Cosmos tenant on the auth-bridge and restart the bridge pod to flush in-memory JWKS. Also we can route Cosmos tenant auth to hosted-identity proxy temporarily (no VPC) as a fallback to restore service quickly.
Maya R: do it. Which is faster?
Samir K: cache clear + bridge restart first — faster and less invasive.
Rachel S: I’ll notify the customer we’re applying a restart and may briefly drop in-flight auth requests.
CosmosAdmin (CosmosHealth): ok go ahead. We can failover to our old tokens if needed but we prefer a platform-side fix.
Samir K: running commands now:
```
# clear jwks cache for tenant cosmos-health
kubectl exec -n cosmos-vpc deploy/auth-bridge -- /usr/local/bin/authctl cache-clear --tenant cosmos-health jwks
kubectl rollout restart deploy/auth-bridge -n cosmos-vpc
```
Samir K: auth-bridge pods restarted, watch logs...
Eli T: I see new fetch to https://id.cosmoshealth.example/.well-known/jwks.json — 200, parsed k2-rot present. Gateway auth start returning 200 again.
Maya R: monitoring — any regressions?
oncall-bot: Incident acknowledged by Maya R at 2134567905
Maya R: customer reports traffic returning to normal. Confirming coroutine job removed the stale cache.
CosmosAdmin (CosmosHealth): we see successful auth across the board now. Thanks.
Maya R: root cause summary so far: customer rotated JWKS (k1->k2), CDN cache headers prevented immediate origin refresh, and our in-memory cache/backoff logic allowed a short window where tokens with new kid failed validation.
Eli T: adding we saw a secondary effect in the dedicated-pool client cert checks — one worker had an expired client cert causing a minority of mTLS handshakes to drop. Not customer-initiated, internal rotation missed that node. We isolated and restarted the pool node.
Maya R: mitigation timeline:
- 07:51 customer rotated JWKS
- ~08:34 first 401s reported to our monitoring
- 08:36 incident-bot paged oncall
- 08:40 cache-clear + auth-bridge restart (2134568040) — auth success resumed 08:42
- 08:55 restarted problematic dedicated pool node (mTLS cert) — resolved 09:01
Samir K: temporary workaround implemented: per-tenant JWKS cache bypass toggle added to auth-bridge config. Turned it on for cosmos-health while we stabilize. Will revert after postmortem.
Rachel S: customer notification sent: "We applied a cache-clear and temporary bypass for JWKS caching. No data exfiltration. Root cause investigation underway."
CosmosAdmin (CosmosHealth): appreciate the live updates. Can you keep the bypass on until we confirm our CDN flushes?
Maya R: yes — will coordinate TTL checks with your infra team. Samir, can we add an active check during key rotations to proactively fetch jwks if we detect kid change for a tenant?
Samir K: action item — implement detection hook: if we receive a token with unknown kid, trigger immediate JWKS fetch bypassing cache for that tenant. Will add to infra backlog with high priority.
Eli T: action item — audit dedicated pool cert rotations and ensure rotation job alerts on any node with expired certs.
Maya R: customer asks for follow-up postmortem and timeline. I’ll own the communication. Samir/Eli, please add fix PRs and link to postmortem.
oncall-bot: Handoff: @Samir K will be primary oncall for the remainder of the war room, @Maya R stepping to support.
Samir K: creating incident ticket and adding required labels.
infra-ops-bot: ticket #INC-2026 created: cosmoshealth-vpc-iam-rotation-stall — assigned samir.k
Maya R: closing loop: service restored, customers notified, mitigation in prod. Postmortem scheduled 48h.
CosmosAdmin (CosmosHealth): thanks everyone — we’ll coordinate CDN cache purge from our side and confirm when done.
Maya R: noted. Postmortem todo (quick):
- add immediate-jwks-fetch on unknown kid (Samir)
- add per-tenant cache-bypass admin toggle with audit (Samir)
- improve rotation runbook for customers with CDN in front of JWKS (Docs) (Product/Rachel)
- cert-rotation alerting for dedicated pools (Eli)
- customer follow-up + timeline (Maya)
Samir K: attaching logs and snippets to the incident ticket. Example error lines:
```
auth-bridge | 2026-06-12T08:35:17Z ERROR jwt validation failed: kid k2-rot not found
gateway     | 2026-06-12T08:35:17Z WARN  auth denied 401 tenant=cosmos-health path=/v1/generate
```
Maya R: good. If there are no further updates, I’ll mark this thread as incident-resolved and start the postmortem doc.
CosmosAdmin (CosmosHealth): confirmed CDN purge completed at 09:20 UTC and we've verified tokens valid. Leave bypass on for 30m then revert.
Maya R: set reminder to revert at 09:50 UTC.
oncall-bot: Incident resolved/mitigated at 2134579400
